jobs.title: Manufacturing Operations Program Manager (Taiwan)
jobs.description:
About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.



Job Summary

Etched is hiring a Manufacturing Operations Program Manager based in Taiwan to lead day-to-day execution at our contract manufacturer. You will serve as the in-region lead responsible for ramping and sustaining production of our core AI hardware, including package assembly and server construction. You’ll work closely with Etched’s production engineering, planning, and supply chain teams to ensure quality, throughput, and readiness at every stage of the build.

This is a hands-on role with direct accountability for factory performance—ideal for someone who thrives in high-volume, precision-oriented environments and enjoys on-the-ground problem-solving.


Key responsibilities

 - Own manufacturing execution at our Taiwan-based Tier 1 contract manufacturer for L6/L10/L11 production, providing day-to-day operational leadership while driving long-term scalability and manufacturing efficiency.

 - Serve as the primary communication bridge between the Taiwan factory and Etched's cross-functional and regional teams, ensuring clear, timely, and effective collaboration.

 - Lead factory capacity planning by tracking equipment readiness and developing mass production (MP) ramp scenarios to support changing business needs.

 - Partner with the contract manufacturer, production planning, and materials teams to develop, optimize, and execute weekly production schedules.

 - Oversee production performance across SMT, mechanical assembly, and test operations, ensuring yield, quality, throughput, and output targets are consistently achieved.

 - Drive cross-functional resolution of manufacturing and technical issues, including DFM/DFx improvements, yield optimization, and rework reduction, in collaboration with Etched and L10/L11 engineering teams.

 - Coordinate new product introduction (NPI) builds, mass production ramps, engineering change orders (ECOs), and process changes to ensure smooth production transitions.

 - Provide real-time visibility into production status by proactively tracking build progress, identifying deviations, escalating risks, and driving timely corrective actions.

 - 

You may be a good fit if you have (Must-have qualifications)

 - 8+ years experience in data center product manufacturing operations, OPM, Contract Manufacturing or TPM roles

 - Track record of working closely with tier 1 CMs in Taiwan or Asia-based fabs

 - Ability to travel regularly to the factory and manage execution in person

 - Excellent communication and bilingual proficiency (Mandarin and English preferred)

 - Skilled at managing escalations, coordinating across time zones, and enforcing timelines

Strong candidates may also have experience with (Nice-to-have qualifications)

 - Engineering background in electrical, mechanical, or packaging domains

 - Exposure to MP ramp planning or cost-of-yield improvement initiatives

Benefits

 - Competitive compensation packages including generous equity packages

 - Comprehensive insurance coverage and other top-of-market benefits

How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose and Taipei, and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both as needed.

Etched is seeking a Manufacturing Design Program Manager to drive technical manufacturing readiness across new product introduction and mass production for our transformer-specific AI systems. This highly cross-functional individual contributor role sits at the intersection of design engineering, test engineering, SMT, FATP, supply chain, and operations. You will lead manufacturing execution from early design-for-manufacturing (DFM) reviews through production ramp, ensuring products are designed for manufacturability and successfully transitioned into high-volume production.

 - Drive manufacturing technical readiness across NPI and mass production in close partnership with hardware design, test engineering, SMT engineering, FATP process engineering, supply chain, and operations teams.

 - Lead DFM reviews across L6, L10, and L11 assemblies, identifying manufacturability risks, integration challenges, and process constraints early in the product development cycle.

 - Own manufacturing readiness for assigned programs, tracking build readiness, factory execution, process capability, yield, schedule, and key manufacturing risks.

 - Coordinate cross-functional execution across prototype, EVT, DVT, PVT, and production builds, ensuring manufacturing deliverables remain on schedule.

 - Partner with contract manufacturers and supply chain teams to develop production plans, line bring-up schedules, tooling readiness, and factory ramp strategies.

 - Drive issue resolution during engineering and production builds through structured root cause analysis and cross-functional coordination.

 - Monitor manufacturing KPIs including yield, cycle time, quality, and factory readiness while driving continuous improvement initiatives.

 - Prepare and communicate manufacturing status, risks, mitigation plans, and execution updates to engineering leadership and executive stakeholders.

 - Partner closely with design engineering to ensure manufacturing considerations are incorporated throughout the product development lifecycle.

 - Travel to domestic and international manufacturing partners as needed to support production readiness and critical builds.



You may be a good fit if you have (Must-have qualifications)

 - 7+ years of experience in hardware engineering, with experience transitioning into Technical Program Management, Design Program Management, or Manufacturing Program Management.

 - Strong preference for candidates with a background in mechanical, electrical, systems, or manufacturing engineering who have led cross-functional hardware programs through NPI and production.

 - Experience managing manufacturing readiness for complex electromechanical systems or high-performance compute hardware.

 - Strong understanding of manufacturing development phases including EVT, DVT, PVT, and production ramp.

 - Experience leading DFM reviews and partnering closely with hardware engineering throughout product development.

 - Experience working directly with contract manufacturers, FATP partners, or ODM/OEM manufacturing operations.

 - Excellent cross-functional program management skills with the ability to coordinate engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and operations teams.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience driving manufacturing issue resolution.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presenting program status, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership.

 - Willingness to work in-person from our San Jose office and travel internationally to manufacturing partners as needed.



Strong candidates may also have experience with (Nice-to-have qualifications)

Experience building AI servers, accelerator systems, networking hardware, storage systems, or other high-performance compute platforms.

Familiarity with SMT manufacturing, factory operations, automated test systems, or final system integration.

Experience with manufacturing yield analytics, SPC methodologies, process capability metrics, or manufacturing data systems.

Experience with liquid-cooled systems, advanced packaging, or high-density compute platforms.

Experience partnering closely with ASIC, systems, thermal, reliability, or validation engineering teams.

Experience working in fast-paced startup environments bringing first-generation hardware products into production.

jobs.title: Silicon Operations Program Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT ETCHED

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




PRODUCTION PLANNING & SCHEDULING

 - Develop and maintain end-to-end production schedules for silicon wafers, interposers, and test/assembly, supporting phases from engineering builds to mass production.

 - Coordinate with foundries, OSATs (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test providers), and internal stakeholders to ensure production milestones and quality goals are met.

 - Collaborate with test engineering teams to coordinate ATE test program development, bring-up planning, and bench validation hardware readiness.

 - Track and forecast capacity planning across all silicon manufacturing stages, including wafer fabrication, component procurement, assembly, and test.
   
   


SUPPLY CHAIN COORDINATION

 - Manage the procurement, delivery, and scheduling of key silicon components (e.g., wafers, interposers, substrates) to ensure optimal time-to-market.

 1. Act as the operational lead between internal teams and suppliers, ensuring transparency and alignment across silicon, packaging, validation, and manufacturing.

 1. Prepare for mass production ramp by ensuring material readiness, test infrastructure availability, and logistic support to mitigate bottlenecks or delays.
    
    


FORECASTING & REPORTING

 - Build and maintain demand forecasts for silicon and related components, based on build plans, yield assumptions, validation schedules, and market dynamics.

 1. Share regular forecasts with supply chain partners and ensure proactive capacity allocation at foundries and OSATs.

 1. Generate and maintain detailed dashboards and reports to track schedule adherence, capacity utilization, inventory status, and delivery performance for executive and technical stakeholders.
    
    


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.

 - 5+ years of experience in supply chain management, production planning, or operations within the semiconductor industry.

 - Deep understanding of the silicon lifecycle: tape-out, fabrication, packaging, test, bring-up, and validation

 - Proven track record working with foundries (TSMC, Samsung, etc.) and OSATs (ASE, Amkor, JCET, etc.).

 - Willingness to travel up to 25% for onsite supplier engagement, engineering builds, and production ramp support.

 - Strong understanding of: Silicon manufacturing processes, including wafer fabrication, dicing, bumping, CoWoS packaging, and testing;

 - Proficiency in using ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle) and advanced Excel skills or analytics tools.

 - Experience with hardware validation cycles and managing silicon hardware logistics.

 - Exceptional program management and organizational skills with the ability to handle complex timelines and interdependencies.

 - Effective communicator and cross-functional leader across engineering, validation, and operations teams.
   
   


STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - Experience working on advanced process nodes (e.g., 5nm, 3nm).

 - Familiarity with ATE platforms (Teradyne, Advantest) and test program infrastructure.

 - Prior experience managing silicon bring-up in hyperscale computing, AI/ML, or high-performance SoC environments.

 - PMP certification or equivalent project/program management training.

 - Familiarity with CoWoS or other 2.5D/3D packaging technologies.



Benefits

 - Full medical, dental, and vision packages, with generous premium coverage

 - Housing subsidy of $2,500/month for those living within walking distance of the office

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)



How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We think most of the progress in the AI field has come from using more FLOPs to train and run models, and the best way to get more FLOPs is to build model-specific hardware. Larger and larger training runs encourage companies to consolidate around fewer model architectures, which creates a market for single-model ASICs.



We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both as needed.

jobs.title: Facilities Engineering Operations Lead, Data Center
jobs.description:
About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.



Job Summary

Etched is building a new category of AI hardware: frontier inference clusters. As our Facilities Engineering Operations Lead, you will own day-to-day operations of our AI data center: uptime, incident response, and escalation across power, cooling, and the white space. You'll be the first hire in this function and will build the operating system from scratch, including procedures, maintenance programs, on-call, and alarming, then turn it into the playbook we copy to every site that follows.



Key Responsibilities

 - Own day-to-day data center operations end to end: uptime, incident response, and escalation for power, cooling, and the white space.

 - Build the operating system from scratch: SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs; change management; preventive and predictive maintenance schedules; shift coverage and on-call; incident and RCA process.

 - Define SLOs and response plans for outage events at the fleet, rack, and server level.

 - Run the liquid cooling plant for high-density racks, including CDUs, secondary fluid loops, water chemistry and filtration, leak detection, and flow and inlet-temperature monitoring.

 - Own electrical operations, including switchgear, busway and PDUs, power connector topology, load balancing across racks, and lockout/tagout (LOTO) and arc-flash safety.

 - Manage electrical, mechanical, CDU OEM, and fire/life safety vendors and contractors: scope work, review quotes, and oversee onsite work.

 - Stand up monitoring and alarming with engineering across BMS/DCIM and rack and CDU telemetry, so problems reach the right person within minutes, not hours.

 - Run rack deployment logistics: receiving, staging, install, commissioning, and turn-up handoff to the hardware and lab teams, plus decommissioning and RMA flows.

 - Track spares and critical parts inventory for facility equipment.

 - Report operational metrics to leadership, including uptime, PUE, incidents, open risks, and capacity headroom.

 - Help build the team, starting with facilities engineering technicians and a BMS specialist.

 - Design processes and site-readiness checklists that can be replicated at our next sites.



You may be a good fit if you have

 - 4-8+ years in critical facilities and data center operations, including time as a Lead or Senior Critical Facilities Engineer or a single-site Facilities Manager

 - Hands-on experience operating liquid cooling in production (CDUs, direct-to-chip / DLC, secondary fluid loops)

 - Deep working knowledge of data center electrical distribution (switchgear, UPS, busway, PDUs) and safe work practices (LOTO, arc flash, NFPA 70E)

 - Experience writing and drilling SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs, and running change management and maintenance programs

 - Experience leading incident response and root cause analysis

 - A track record of managing mechanical, electrical, and fire/life safety vendors

 - Working knowledge of BMS, DCIM, and power monitoring systems

 - Readiness to own the whole site, not just a shift or a system

 - Deeply creative and able to think from first principles



Strong candidates may also have experience with

 - Running high-density GPU / AI infrastructure at a neocloud, hyperscaler, or colocation provider

 - Standing up a new site or data hall, including commissioning and turn-up

 - Building and staffing 24/7 operations and on-call rotations

 - Familiarity with modern ML and LLM model architectures

 - Ability to program with Python or another scripting language

 - Familiarity with AI tools for programming/coding

 - Startup experience or comfort working in fast-paced environments



Benefits

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage

 - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

 - Housing subsidy of $2k per month for those living within walking distance of the office

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

 - Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification



How we're different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.



We greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.
